title: Vayera: Isaac is born (Genesis 21:1–7)
hook: God remembers Sarah, and she says all who hear will laugh with her

segments.voice: Yesterday, a foreign king in Gerar turned out more upright than Abraham feared. Your line was goodness is everywhere. Today, a promise twenty-five years long comes true.

There are two kinds of laughter. One is the short, dry laugh when someone tells you something impossible. Oh, sure. Right. That'll never happen. The other bursts out of you when the impossible thing happens anyway. The baby is born. The test comes back clear. The person you gave up on walks through the door. Almost the same sound, from a completely different place. Sarah laughs both ways in this portion. Today, the second laugh.
screen: `OH, SURE. RIGHT.` → `THE IMPOSSIBLE HAPPENS ANYWAY.` → `SARAH LAUGHS BOTH WAYS.`

segments.voice: A few chapters back, three visitors came to Abraham's tent, and one said: this time next year, Sarah will have a son. Sarah, about ninety, was listening from inside the tent. She laughed to herself: after I'm worn out, and my husband is old, shall I have pleasure? God asked Abraham: why did Sarah laugh? "Is any thing too hard for the LORD?" Sarah, afraid, said, I didn't laugh. The answer came back: no, you did laugh. That was the first laugh. Now, chapter twenty-one. God remembered Sarah, as promised, and did for her as God had spoken. In her old age, at exactly the time foretold, she gives birth to a son. Abraham names him Yitzchak, Isaac, which means he will laugh. And Sarah says: God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me. Then, almost in wonder: who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? The same laugh, turned inside out, from disbelief to joy. And she doesn't keep it to herself. Rashi, following the midrash, says that when Sarah was remembered, many other childless women were remembered with her, many sick people were healed, many prayers were answered, and there was laughter in the whole world. This chapter is read in synagogues on the first day of Rosh Hashanah; the tradition says Sarah was remembered on that day. So every Jewish year begins with a laugh that turned from doubt to joy.
screen: `SARAH LAUGHED TO HERSELF.` · `IS ANY THING TOO HARD FOR THE LORD?` · `YITZCHAK: HE WILL LAUGH.` · `LAUGHTER IN THE WHOLE WORLD.` · then, large: `LAUGH WITH ME.`

segments.voice: Think of a time something you'd given up on actually happened, big or small, and remember the laugh or the smile that came out of you. Let it come back into your face now, even a little. Then picture the people you'd want to share it with, and let the joy spread out to them: everyone who hears will laugh with me.
Vayera. The portion where Sarah's laugh of disbelief becomes a laugh of joy, and her son is named Isaac, he will laugh.
Your line: laugh with me. Her laugh had room for everyone. Day one hundred seventy-nine, done.

howItsDone: Genesis 21 is read in synagogues on the first day of Rosh Hashanah, when, tradition says, Sarah was remembered; the birth of Isaac is often taught alongside Sarah's two laughs.

fork.setup: you're Sarah. you've finally given birth, at about ninety. what do you say?
options: don't tell anyone; they'll laugh at me.

fork.reveal: Sarah turns the laugh outward: everyone who hears will laugh with me. the laugh of doubt becomes a laugh of joy.

chat.says: Is Sarah's laugh in the Torah a good thing or a bad thing?
options: Both: first a laugh of doubt, then, when Isaac is born, a laugh of joy she shares.
Only bad: she laughed once, denied it, and the Torah never brings it up again.
Only good: she laughed for joy the very moment the visitors spoke.
chat.meaning: Sarah laughed in doubt at the promise. At Isaac's birth the same laugh turned to joy: everyone who hears will laugh with me.

Yitzchak.meaning: Isaac's Hebrew name; it means he will laugh

Rashi.meaning: a great medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud

midrash.meaning: rabbinic stories and teachings that read between the Torah's lines

Rosh Hashanah.meaning: the Jewish New Year, when this chapter is read
